title: Private deployment: credential rotation race caused RBAC resolution failures and missing audit entries
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: A subset of customers on Private deployments experienced RBAC failures after an automated credential/KMS rotation job briefly produced inconsistent key material across the runtime group. The inconsistency caused two production issues: (1) RBAC role resolution would fail intermittently for some service accounts because the token validation path couldn't decrypt role bindings; (2) audit logging for affected requests was dropped or truncated while the decryption error path attempted fallback, causing gaps in audit trails. Multiple customers escalated with outages and missing audit evidence. This ticket tracks the urgent patch, verification, and longer-term fixes.
steps_to_reproduce: Spin up private runtime cluster with customer KMS integration configured (customer-managed key).
Trigger automated KMS key rotation flow (simulate rotation event where two rotation workers overlap by ~10-30s).
Send concurrent authenticated requests that exercise RBAC role lookup and token decryption (high QPS, >500 rps).
Observe logs: decryption errors in runtime-auth service and missing/partial entries in audit sink for a narrow time window.
mitigation_and_workaround: Immediate: Roll forward emergency hotpatch (PR #github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/1459) to make rotation job perform coordinated handoff using a leader lease — reduces crossover window to <1s.

Temporary: For affected customers, enable 'legacy-key-fallback' in the private control plane (applies only to VPC/private deployments) to allow token validation using previous key for 10 minutes after rotation.
Customer comms: Notified impacted tenants with steps to preserve logs and provided manual audit exports for the affected time window.
root_cause_summary: A race in the credential rotation controller caused two workers to populate different active key metadata in the runtime cache. The runtime-auth path attempted to decrypt role-binding payloads with the new key while some nodes still had cached entries encrypted with the old key. The error handling path dropped audit payloads when decryption failed and the retry/backoff logic resumed requests without emitting full audit objects. Contributing factors: lack of an atomic metadata swap, insufficient leader election guard, and audit pipeline not durable to decryption transient failures.
fix_plan: 1) Hotpatch rotation controller to require a leader lease and perform a coordinated two-phase commit for key metadata publication (short-term patch). PR: github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/1459

2) Add idempotent metadata retrieval with new key hinting to runtime-auth so nodes can attempt previous key decryption before failing requests (short-term patch). PR: github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/1463
3) Improve audit sink to persist encryption-failure rows to a retry queue instead of dropping them; add observability for transient decrypt failures (medium-term).
4) Long-term: rework KMS rotation flow to publish rotation epoch and require nodes to observe the epoch change via consensus (etcd) before switching active key for RPCs.
deployment_plan: Stage the hotpatch to dedicated canary environments (canary=2 nodes) in the staging VPC, run synthetic RBAC+KMS rotation tests for 30 minutes, then promote to affected private customers in batches (10 customers per batch) with a 15-minute observation window. Emergency rollback: revert to previous rotation-controller image and re-enable legacy-key-fallback. Engineering on-call will coordinate with SEs during customer rollouts.
verification_steps: Run the rotation race reproduction harness (tests/rotation_race.py) against the patched controller for 100K simulated rotations — expect 0 cross-key decryption errors.
Smoke test RBAC flows across 3 runtime regions for each customer batch (create role-binding, get token, validate request).
Verify audit sink has no gaps for the test timeframe and that previously-truncated payloads are present in retry queue and processed.
Confirm with at least two impacted customers that their incoming requests succeed and that audit logs for the previous incident window were provided.
